source.author: cic
source.text: sequor igitur eas vias quas didici ab Antiocho, nec reperio quo modo iudicem si lucet, lucet verum esse ob eam causam quod ita didici, omne quod ipsum ex se conexum sit verum esse, non iudicem si mentiris, mentiris eodem modo esse conexum: aut igitur hoc ut illud, aut nisi hoc ne illud quidem iudicabo.
source.text_original: sequor igitur eas vias quas didici ab Antiocho, nec reperio quo modo iudicem 'si lucet, lucet' verum esse ob eam causam quod ita didici, omne quod ipsum ex se conexum sit verum esse, non iudicem 'si mentiris, mentiris' eodem modo esse conexum: aut igitur hoc ut illud, aut nisi hoc ne illud quidem iudicabo.
source.text_english: So I follow those lines of argument which I learned from Antiochus, and I do not see how I could judge, if it is clear that it is true for this reason, that is how I learned it, that everything which is connected in itself from itself is true, while I do not judge that if you are lying, you are lying in the same way is connected: either therefore I shall judge this just as that, or unless I judge this, then not even that.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: si mentiris idque uerum dicis, mentiris et in memet reuersus conuerti in aduersarium propositionis stropham.
reuse.text_original: 'si mentiris idque uerum dicis, mentiris' et in memet reuersus conuerti in aduersarium propositionis stropham.
reuse.text_english: If you are lying and yet say that this is true, you are lying; and, turning back upon myself, I have turned into an opponent through the trickery of the proposition.
